results.productionHelperRefusal: Codex cannot enforce the chat tool policy: a personal stdio MCP named cinna conflicts with the chat connector; rename that MCP server. Choose Claude or OpenCode for this chat, or use the verified Codex CLI version.

boundaries: Every model response is generated by a loopback deterministic Responses fixture. No credentials or personal profile were copied, inherited, or modified.
39 checks passed, including two expected fail-closed stdio collisions: scratch adapter session creation and production helper preparation.

Scratch adapter comparisons reconstruct the original MCP merge and the maintained merge without editing the installed adapter. Production-helper cases transpile the actual helper into scratch, use real config discovery and generated artifacts, and drive the installed digest-verified adapter.

All 11 bundled model slugs were checked with transformed metadata. Native-action feature flags, disabled web search and inherited MCP disables must apply at both process startup and thread configuration; testing only the initial main session missed auxiliary model requests after resume/model changes.

No-MCP Default-mode sessions expose one schema (request_user_input), whose valid invocation is rejected as unavailable. Fabricated set_collaboration_mode calls are unsupported. This is no usable tool action, not a zero-schema assertion.

Same-process session/load preserved a Plan mode fixture until explicit Default setup. Resumed requests, actual model changes and auxiliary model requests retained the restricted tool sets. Cross-process resume remains unverified.

The production helper generated an identical process key/wrapper for chat and title prompts. Actual separate session directories in one process received distinct exact developer/system instructions; title had no chat prompt, no user-prefix instruction and no usable tool.

Empty MCP maps and startup CLI disables alone did not isolate inherited providers after adapter session configuration. The maintained merge preserves explicit thread disables. Literal dotted, quoted, semicolon and newline MCP names were disabled safely with a quoted-key inline TOML table.
A same-name HTTP entry, including disabled, works when the injected endpoint is explicitly enabled and adapter name filtering is disabled. A same-name stdio entry is refused before any model request.
guardian_approval and enable_request_compression overrides were removed and the final matrix passed; they are not part of the no-native-action policy.
Unknown explicit model slugs must be rejected by application policy; the engine itself accepts unknown slugs.
No account authentication, real-provider quality/billing, cross-process resume, cancellation or list-change behavior was established by this Codex probe.
